purpose: Implements Critical CSS Generation — extracts and inlines above-the-fold CSS in <head>, defers full stylesheets, stores per-template CCSS files, generates via Action Scheduler, runs daily cron regeneration, and adds React UI toggle in File Optimization > Assets.
riskRationale: All 24 previously reported issues from iteration 1 have been verified as fixed. One new critical bug (undefined array key $html_match[1]) silently drops CSS custom properties from html selector during extraction but does not cause data loss or security issues. No security concerns remain.
breakingChanges: New dependency on DOMDocument PHP extension

text: The implementation is solid and well-integrated with the existing plugin architecture. All 24+ issues from the previous review iteration have been addressed — brace-depth parser with string-context tracking, DOMDocument guards, self-fetch recursion protection, namespace resolution, and race conditions are all resolved. One new critical bug was introduced: accessing $html_match[1] on a regex without capturing groups, which silently excludes CSS custom property definitions on the html element from critical CSS and triggers PHP 8.2+ warnings.

reasoning: One critical bug (undefined array key $html_match[1] at line 592) blocks merge — CSS custom properties on html are silently dropped from critical CSS, and PHP 8.2+ warnings fire. All other findings are pre-existing minor issues from iteration 1 that do not block merge.

message: The WPPO_GENERATING_CCSS define guard effectively prevents self-fetch recursion during background generation — a well-designed protection against cascading HTTP requests.

The brace-depth parser with string-context tracking handles the full complexity of minified CSS (nested braces, data URIs, string literals) correctly — a significant improvement over the initial [^}]+ regex approach.

Custom page template resolution via get_page_template_slug() ensures correct hash generation for templates like 'page-about.php' — fixing the mismatch that prevented CCSS from being served for custom templates.

First-visit trigger pattern in inline_ccss() correctly avoids FOUC: no CCSS file → no inline CSS, no deferral, async job queued. Second visit gets the benefit. This is the correct progressive enhancement approach.
Configurable size cap (default 50KB) with error_log warning when exceeded, plus wp_strip_all_tags() sanitization on inline output — closes both the bloat and XSS vectors elegantly.

Well-designed heuristic CSS extraction with token-based matching (token_match) that properly prevents substring false-positives (e.g., '.container' not matching '.container-fluid'). The brace-depth parser handles minified CSS correctly.
Clean delegation of CCSS clearing from Cache::delete_all_cache_files() to Cache::clear_ccss() → Critical_CSS::clear_all(), eliminating the duplicate hardcoded template list.

Undefined array key $html_match[1]. The regex '/html\s*\{((?:[^{}]|\{[^{}]*\})*)\}/i' has no capturing groups (the outer group is wrapped but the inner (?:...) is non-capturing), yet $html_match[1] is accessed. This triggers PHP 8.2+ E_WARNING every time the html selector has CSS custom properties. The condition also always evaluates to false (null !== false), so CSS variables defined on html (common in block themes) are NEVER included in critical CSS, potentially breaking above-fold rendering that depends on custom properties.
suggestion: Add a capturing group around the rule body content by wrapping the non-capturing group in parentheses.

message: The @import regex does not handle media-qualified imports like @import url('style.css') screen; or @import 'style.css' screen and (min-width: 768px);. These imports are silently skipped during inlining.
suggestion: Extend the regex to optionally consume the media query portion after the closing quote/paren: (?:['"]?\s+[^;]*)? before the semicolon.

message: SKIP_DEFER_HANDLES constant name is misleading — it is used for both exact handle matching ($handle === $skip) and URL substring matching (strpos($href, $skip)) in defer_stylesheets() and for URL substring matching in generate(). The name implies it only holds handle names.
suggestion: Rename to SKIP_DEFER_ITEMS and update the doc comment to clarify matching semantics.

message: Only max-width media queries are extracted. Desktop-critical layout rules wrapped in min-width queries are excluded, which could cause desktop visitors to experience FOUC or missing layout on wider viewports.
suggestion: Also include min-width media queries alongside the max-width extraction for balanced mobile-first and desktop coverage.

message: The Cache::clear_ccss() static method's fallback path (new self() with filesystem-only cleanup) is dead code since Critical_CSS is always loaded. If it ever executes, it deletes the CCSS directory without clearing status transients, leaving stale 'ready' transients that would cause the UI to show generated status for nonexistent files.
suggestion: Remove the fallback entirely. If kept for safety, add a delete_transient call for each template hash in the fallback path.

message: The token_match() regex has $ inside the character class [.#:\s\[>+~)\]|$] where it is interpreted as a literal $ character, not an end-of-string anchor. The | is also literal inside a character class. Selectors ending with $ would cause incorrect matching.
suggestion: Move the end-of-string assertion outside the character class using an alternation: (?=[.#:\s\[>+~)\]|]|$).

message: resolve_import_url() doesn't normalize .. path components. A relative import like ../fonts/font.css against base https://example.com/theme/style.css produces https://example.com/theme/../fonts/font.css instead of https://example.com/fonts/font.css. WordPress's HTTP API handles this, but the cache hash becomes unpredictable.
suggestion: Add path normalization after URL construction that collapses .. segments.

message: resolve_inline_imports() appends resolved @import content to the original content but never removes the original @import statements. This bloats intermediate CSS with duplicate selectors that need to be filtered out during above-fold extraction, wasting processing.
suggestion: Replace the @import line with its resolved content using preg_replace instead of appending, or strip @import lines after collecting their content.

message: The regenerate_ccss REST endpoint calls Critical_CSS::regenerate_all() unconditionally without checking whether the criticalCSS setting is enabled. If called when disabled, it queues background jobs that generate CCSS files that will never be served.
suggestion: Add a guard to check the criticalCSS setting before queuing regeneration jobs.
